books.name: Hosea
gists: Hosea marries Gomer, symbolizing Israel's unfaithfulness and future restoration.
God announces Israel's unfaithfulness, threatens judgment, but promises future restoration.
Hosea redeems his unfaithful wife, symbolizing God's love and Israel's future restoration.
Israel is condemned for sin, idolatry, and lack of faithfulness.
God judges Israel for sin, pride, and spiritual unfaithfulness.
God calls Israel to return, seeking mercy over sacrifice and healing.
Israel's sins and corrupt leaders prevent healing despite God's efforts.
God warns Israel of judgment for idolatry and covenant breach.
Israel's unfaithfulness leads to exile, desolation, and divine judgment.
Israel faces ruin due to idolatry and divided hearts.
The LORD remembers His love for rebellious Israel despite their idolatry.
Ephraim's alliances provoke God's judgment, urging Israel towards mercy and justice.
Ephraim's idolatry leads to destruction despite God's warnings and promise.
Israel is urged to return to the LORD for healing and guidance.

anchors.text: For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.

books.name: Joel
gists: A locust plague devastates the land, prompting mourning and a call to fast.
A trumpet signals the LORD’s impending judgment and calls for repentance.
God will judge nations and restore Jerusalem and Judah.

anchors.text: And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions:

books.name: Amos
gists: Amos proclaims judgment on neighboring nations for their cruelty and betrayal.
God judges Moab, Judah, and Israel for injustice, idolatry, and rejection.
God warns Israel of impending judgment due to sin and injustice.
Israel's leaders face judgment for oppression and unrepentant luxury.
God urges Israel to seek Him and embrace justice, warning of judgment.
God condemns Israel's pride and warns of impending destruction.
Amos receives visions of judgment, affirming Israel’s sins and Amaziah's downfall.
Amos predicts Israel's doom and a famine of God's word.
God promises judgment on Israel but assures future restoration and prosperity.

anchors.text: But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.
Behold, the days come, saith the Lord GOD, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD:

books.name: Obadiah
gists: Edom is judged for pride and violence against Israel; Jacob will prevail.

anchors.text: For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.

books.name: Jonah
gists: Jonah flees to Tarshish, causing a storm, and is swallowed by a fish.
Jonah prays from the fish, vows thanks, and is saved by God.
Jonah preaches in Nineveh, the people repent, and God spares them.
Jonah pouts over God's mercy; learns compassion through a withering gourd.

anchors.text: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.

books.name: Micah
gists: Micah prophesies judgment against Samaria and Jerusalem for their sins.
God condemns land seizers and false prophets, promising to restore Israel.
Corrupt leaders and false prophets deceive, facing God's impending judgment.
The LORD promises peace and restoration for Zion and the nations.
A ruler from Bethlehem will lead Israel and defeat enemies.
God calls Israel to accountability, emphasizing justice over rituals.
The prophet laments deceit but trusts God’s justice and restoration.

anchors.text: But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

books.name: Nahum
gists: God declares vengeance against Nineveh while offering refuge to Judah.
Nineveh faces siege and destruction as its power crumbles.
Nineveh faces imminent destruction for its violence and sinfulness.

anchors.text: The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.

books.name: Habakkuk
gists: Habakkuk questions God about violence and injustice, receiving answers about judgment.
Habakkuk is instructed to write the vision and warns of judgment.
Habakkuk praises God’s power and resolves to trust despite devastation.

anchors.text: Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.
Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation.

books.name: Zephaniah
gists: Zephaniah declares impending judgment on Judah for idolatry and wickedness.
Nations face judgment; seek the Lord for refuge and righteousness.
Jerusalem faces judgment, yet the LORD promises restoration and joy.

anchors.text: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.

books.name: Haggai
gists: Haggai encourages rebuilding the temple, urging obedience and promising blessings.
Haggai encourages rebuilding the temple, promising greater future glory.

anchors.text: Now therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts; Consider your ways.

books.name: Zechariah
gists: Zechariah calls for repentance, promising mercy and restoration for Jerusalem.
A man measures Jerusalem, and God's protection and restoration are promised.
Joshua is cleansed and assured of God's promise despite Satan's accusation.
Zechariah sees a vision assuring Zerubbabel of God's support for rebuilding.
A flying scroll and a woman symbolize judgment and removal of wickedness.
Four chariots symbolize God's spirits, and Joshua is crowned as priest-king.
God questions the fasting motives, urging true compassion and justice.
God promises peace and prosperity in Jerusalem, uniting nations under His presence.
Judgment on nations, humble king bringing salvation to Zion.
The LORD promises restoration, rain, and safety for His people.
The prophet depicts judgment by rejecting unfaithful shepherds and receiving silver.
God will protect Jerusalem and bring mourning for the pierced one.
A fountain cleanses sin, false prophets are removed, and a remnant is refined.
Nations attack Jerusalem, but the LORD triumphs, restoring the city.

anchors.text: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.

Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.
And the LORD shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one LORD, and his name one.

books.name: Malachi
gists: God loves Israel, rejects Edom, and rebukes priests for corrupt sacrifices.
God rebukes corrupt priests and condemns Judah's treachery in marriage.
The LORD promises a messenger and rebukes Judah for unfaithfulness.
The LORD promises judgment for the proud and healing for the righteous.

anchors.text: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the LORD of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.
But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.
